Stage 2a: two-country linked pilot

Germany and France in one koma system – proving the linkage mechanism before scaling to eleven

1. The system

Everything below is a single koma::system_of_equations() call: 21 equations, 13 stochastic and 8 identities, no external packages and no per-country loop over estimate().

de_consumption~constant+de_gdp+de_consumption.L(1),
de_investment~constant+de_gdp+de_long_rate+de_investment.L(1),
de_exports~constant+de_foreign_demand+de_exports.L(1),
de_imports~constant+de_domestic_demand+de_imports.L(1),
de_prices~constant+eur_usd+oil_price+de_prices.L(1),
de_long_rate~constant+de_prices+ea_policy_rate+de_gdp+de_long_rate.L(1),
fr_consumption~constant+fr_gdp+fr_consumption.L(1),
fr_investment~constant+fr_gdp+fr_long_rate+fr_investment.L(1),
fr_exports~constant+fr_foreign_demand+fr_exports.L(1),
fr_imports~constant+fr_domestic_demand+fr_imports.L(1),
fr_prices~constant+eur_usd+oil_price+fr_prices.L(1),
fr_long_rate~constant+fr_prices+ea_policy_rate+fr_gdp+fr_long_rate.L(1),
ea_policy_rate~constant+ea_prices+ea_gdp+ea_policy_rate.L(1),
de_gdp==0.937*de_domestic_demand+0.369*de_exports-0.314*de_imports,
de_domestic_demand==0.585*de_consumption+0.211*de_investment+0.204*de_government,
de_foreign_demand==0.065*fr_gdp+0.935*row_gdp,
fr_gdp==0.988*fr_domestic_demand+0.291*fr_exports-0.284*fr_imports,
fr_domestic_demand==0.545*fr_consumption+0.218*fr_investment+0.237*fr_government,
fr_foreign_demand==0.139*de_gdp+0.861*row_gdp,
ea_gdp==0.604*de_gdp+0.396*fr_gdp,
ea_prices==0.604*de_prices+0.396*fr_prices

Three things differ from stage 1, and each is deliberate:

  1. Exports are driven by <iso2>_foreign_demand, a fixed-weight identity over the other country’s endogenous GDP. Stage 1 used the exogenous row_gdp, which excludes every modelled economy — so intra-EA export demand was missing entirely.
  2. ea_policy_rate is endogenous, with a Taylor-type rule over GDP-weighted ea_gdp / ea_prices identities.
  3. <iso2>_long_rate enters investment. This is what actually gives the policy rate a route to GDP — see §4.

Endogenous vs exogenous, as koma parses them

How koma parses the system. Note identity left-hand sides are endogenous.
n variables
endogenous 21 de_consumption, de_investment, de_exports, de_imports, de_prices, de_long_rate, fr_consumption, fr_investment, fr_exports, fr_imports, fr_prices, fr_long_rate, ea_policy_rate, de_gdp, de_domestic_demand, de_foreign_demand, fr_gdp, fr_domestic_demand, fr_foreign_demand, ea_gdp, ea_prices
stochastic equations 13 de_consumption, de_investment, de_exports, de_imports, de_prices, de_long_rate, fr_consumption, fr_investment, fr_exports, fr_imports, fr_prices, fr_long_rate, ea_policy_rate
identities 8 de_gdp, de_domestic_demand, de_foreign_demand, fr_gdp, fr_domestic_demand, fr_foreign_demand, ea_gdp, ea_prices
exogenous 5 eur_usd, oil_price, de_government, row_gdp, fr_government
predetermined 13 de_consumption.L1, de_investment.L1, de_exports.L1, de_imports.L1, de_prices.L1, de_long_rate.L1, fr_consumption.L1, fr_investment.L1, fr_exports.L1, fr_imports.L1, fr_prices.L1, fr_long_rate.L1, ea_policy_rate.L1

The exogenous set is five, not the three truly-global variables. <iso2>_government has no equation of its own (fiscal policy is a given, as in stage 1) but does appear in the domestic-demand identities. koma’s validate_completeness() is an exact-set check — an undeclared variable aborts, and so does a declared-but-unused one — so this set is neither a subset nor a superset of what is used.

Linkage weights

Each modelled partner keeps its true W_trade weight; everything else lumps into row_gdp.
identity weights
de_foreign_demand fr_gdp 0.065, row_gdp 0.935
fr_foreign_demand de_gdp 0.139, row_gdp 0.861
ea_gdp / ea_prices de 0.604, fr 0.396

Documented approximation. build_row_gdp() excludes all eleven modelled economies by construction, so in a two-country pilot the 0.935 weight on row_gdp is proxying the nine absent modelled partners (0.374 of German trade) as well as genuine rest-of-world. This shrinks monotonically as countries are added — each new country claims its own W_trade weight out of the row residual, and no other weight is rescaled.

The immediate consequence is that the DE↔︎FR channel is small by construction: France is only 6.5% of German trade. §5 shows that this is exactly what the estimates say.

The four constructed series

koma::estimate() requires a series for every endogenous variable, identity- defined ones included, and only says so from inside estimate(). Four have no observed counterpart: de_foreign_demand, fr_foreign_demand, ea_gdp, ea_prices.

They are built with chain_weighted_index(), not apply_weights(), because koma estimates on growth rates: an identity is a statement about diff(log()), and log(0.6a + 0.4b) != 0.6*log(a) + 0.4*log(b). A level-space aggregate would leave the estimator reading one relationship out of the data while the identity’s Gamma column encodes another — silently, since koma performs no identity-consistency check. For de_foreign_demand the two constructions differ by up to 13.7 percentage points of quarterly growth. The chained version reproduces its identity to 8.5e-14.

2. Pre-flight

All checks run before committing to estimation.
check ok detail
identity RHS variables all resolve TRUE -
no variable defined twice TRUE -
every variable has a panel series TRUE 26 variables present
no internal NAs in required series TRUE -
identities declared last TRUE 13 stochastic then 8 identities
system identified TRUE 10/10 seeds pass order + rank

model_identification() fills free coefficients with rnorm draws, so a single pass proves very little — it is repeated across 10 seeds, and passes the order and rank conditions on all of them.

The “identities declared last” check is not cosmetic. koma assumes it positionally in two places (model_identification() loops for (j in seq(1, n_endogenous - n_identities)) over columns, and estimate_sem() indexes y_matrix[, jx] by the same index), so an identity declared anywhere else makes koma estimate the wrong columns and mislabel the results with no error. This is undocumented; every example koma ships obeys it.

4. Does the policy rate reach GDP?

The stage-1 diagnostics report closed on a structural finding: a policy-rate shock could not move GDP, because long_rate was a terminal satellite equation. Making ea_policy_rate endogenous does not on its own fix that — traced on the contemporaneous Gamma graph, a policy rate with no investment channel reaches only de_long_rate and fr_long_rate, and stops.

Adding <iso2>_long_rate to the investment equation is what closes the loop:

Contemporaneous reachability on the Gamma matrix.
from reaches includes_fr_gdp detail
ea_policy_rate 17 TRUE de_consumption, de_domestic_demand, de_exports, de_foreign_demand, de_gdp, de_imports, de_investment, de_long_rate, ea_gdp, fr_consumption, fr_domestic_demand, fr_exports, fr_foreign_demand, fr_gdp, fr_imports, fr_investment, fr_long_rate
de_gdp 17 TRUE (full cycle)

The cross-country cycle asked for is present and closed: de_gdp → fr_foreign_demand → fr_exports → fr_gdp → de_foreign_demand → de_exports → de_gdp.

Is that well-posed? Yes, and estimation and forecasting stress different things:

  • Estimation is limited-information and equation-by-equation (draw_parameters_j). Contemporaneous endogenous regressors are read from the observed y_matrix; koma never inverts Gamma while sampling. A cycle is the ordinary simultaneous-equations case. The binding constraint is identification, checked symbolically before any data is touched — and it passes.
  • Forecasting is where a bad loop would bite: the reduced form is B %*% solve(Gamma), so Gamma must be invertible. Measured det(Gamma) stays in 0.31–1.11 across rate→investment coefficients of −10…+5 and Taylor gains 0…5. The economically-correct negative rate→investment sign moves it away from singularity, since a negative feedback loop is stabilising.

Had it not been well-posed there would have been three distinct failure modes: under-identification aborts up front (cheap, loud); a singular Gamma throws a bare base-R solve() error at forecast time; and a near-singular Gamma throws nothing at all and silently returns explosive forecasts. koma has no cycle, stability or eigenvalue check anywhere, so the third is the dangerous one. Here the cross-country loop gain is ≈0.369 × 0.065 × 0.291 × 0.139 ≈ 0.001 — three orders of magnitude from 1.

Where they differ, and why

Three distinct patterns, and the mechanism for each is visible in koma’s sampler rather than inferred:

prices does not move at all (deltas 0.000–0.006, i.e. Monte Carlo noise). It is the one equation with no contemporaneous endogenous regressor, so draw_omega_j takes its number_endogenous_in_j == 0 branch, which uses only the equation’s own restricted regressor columns. Nothing about the wider system can reach it. This is a useful control: it confirms the differences elsewhere are a real estimation effect and not a change of sample, vintage or seed handling.

consumption moves slightly (de_gdp +0.007, fr_gdp +0.059).

imports moves most — de_domestic_demand 0.059 → 0.743, fr_domestic_demand 1.725 → 2.633.

The mechanism is the instrument set, not the trade loop. koma’s sampler is limited-information, but the gamma block of any equation with a contemporaneous endogenous regressor is drawn from a target that projects on the full x_matrix. Stage 1 gave Germany 12 columns; stage 2a gives 19:

added to the projection for every equation:
   fr_consumption.L1, fr_investment.L1, fr_exports.L1, fr_imports.L1, fr_prices.L1, fr_long_rate.L1, ea_policy_rate.L1, fr_government 

estimation sample unchanged: stage 1 n = 78  stage 2a n = 78

Imports move most because <iso2>_domestic_demand is the most weakly identified contemporaneous regressor in the stage-1 system — Germany’s stage-1 estimate was 0.059 with a 90% interval of [−1.05, 1.18], essentially uninformative — so it is the coefficient with the most room to move when the instrument set widens. Note the interval does not tighten (it widens slightly, to [−0.53, 2.03]): this is a shift in location, not a gain in precision, and the two estimates remain mutually consistent.

The headline is the null result. No coefficient in a structurally identical equation moved outside its stage-1 90% interval. That is the honest reading of a two-country pilot with w_de_fr = 0.065: the mechanism works, the cycle is closed and identified, and it changes almost nothing yet — which is what a loop gain of 0.001 predicts. The linkage becomes economically material only as countries are added and the row_gdp residual is replaced by modelled partners.

All signed as theory expects: export elasticities on foreign demand are positive (DE 0.96, FR 1.67); the rate→investment channel is negative in both countries (DE −0.111, FR −0.076), though both intervals straddle zero; and the Taylor rule loads positively on both ea_prices (0.268) and ea_gdp (0.203) with a near-unit-root lag (0.995). The ea_policy_rate equation’s own acceptance rate, 39.3%, sits comfortably mid-band.

6. Verdict

The mechanism works. The cross-country contemporaneous cycle is expressible in one system_of_equations(), is identified on every seed tried, and yields an invertible Gamma with a large margin. Acceptance rates are in band after one tuning round. Every new coefficient is correctly signed.

Two caveats to carry into stage 2b:

  • The pilot’s economic content is small. With France at 6.5% of German trade and 93.5% of German foreign demand riding on a row_gdp series that excludes the nine other modelled economies, the linkage cannot do much yet. Nothing here validates the magnitude of cross-country transmission — only the mechanism.
  • The rate→investment channel is not sharply estimated. Both coefficients are correctly signed but their 90% intervals include zero. The channel exists structurally; whether it is strong enough to make a policy-rate conditional forecast meaningful is a question for the conditional-forecast checks, not this report.

Eight-quarter forecast

8 quarters from 2023Q1 to 2024Q4, 1000 posterior draws. The whole window is already observed, so this is an out-of-sample check rather than a projection.

Every fan below is the filtered predictive interval: koma constrains no draw to be stationary, so a draw whose quarterly growth exceeds 100% in absolute value is dropped before the quantiles are taken, exactly as score_forecast() does when it scores a backtest. The solid band is the 25th-75th percentile of what survives, the faint band the 10th-90th, the dark line their median, and the grey line the realised path where one exists. Across the variables shown, 0.0% of draws are discarded as explosive at horizon 1, rising to 0.0% at horizon 8 (worst: de_gdp at 0.0%). A variable whose discarded share climbs steeply is one whose fan understates the model’s true uncertainty, so read the tail of a wide fan as an ordering rather than a number.

The panels are clipped, and that is worth saying plainly. Eight quarters out, the 10-90 interval on quarterly growth spans tens of percentage points in every stage of this project – an honest number, and one that makes the median invisible if the axis is scaled to contain it. Each panel is therefore scaled to its inner band, and the outer band runs to the panel edge rather than being drawn in full. Nothing is concealed: the table at the end of this section reports the untruncated bounds.

The level paths are anchored on conditionally-filled values, not observed ones. koma takes the anchor from the end of the fit’s own ts_data, and this stage fills 2022Q4 before forecasting. The worst discrepancy is de_prices, anchored at 85.02 against an observed 93.55 – -9.1% out – and the median across all variables is 1.2%. A level gap at horizon 1 is therefore inherited from the fill, not produced by the forecast. Read the rate chart, which is unaffected.

A forecast this long needs the exogenous series to reach the end of the horizon, and they do not: every one of them stops at the fit’s own native forecast end. extend_forecast_horizon() carries each one forward on its trailing four-quarter average growth – a momentum continuation, not a view on oil markets or world trade – and koma would otherwise have silently returned a shorter horizon than the one requested.
